title: नेपाली व्याकरण शिक्षण प्रक्रियाको निरूपण
nepali: नेपाली व्याकरण शिक्षण प्रक्रियाको निरूपण’ शीर्षकको प्रस्तुत अनुसन्धानमूलक लेख अनुसन्धाता स्वयम्द्वारा लिखित ‘स्नातक तहमा व्याकरण शिक्षण प्रक्रियाको अवस्था’ शीर्षकको लघु अनुसन्धान प्रतिवेदनको सङ्क्षिप्त एवम् परिमार्जित रूप हो । यस लेखमा स्नातक तहमा व्याकरण शिक्षण प्रक्रियाको अवस्था पहिल्याउने रउक्त शिक्षण प्रक्रिया स्नातक नेपाली शिक्षण निर्देशिका (२०६६) र स्नातक नेपाली पाठ्यक््रmम (२०६९) ले निर्देश गरेअनुसार रचनामुखी एवम् सम्पे्रषणात्मक किसिमले भए नभएको निरूपण गर्ने उद्देश्य राखिएको छ । यो लेख एकल सत्यमा आधारित गुणमात्रात्मक प्रकृतिको भएकाले यसका लागि कास्की जिल्लाका स्नातक तहमा अध्यापन गर्ने १० जना शिक्षक र उनीहरूका व्याकरण शिक्षणसँग सम्बन्धित १० वटा कक्षालाई नमुना जनसङ्ख्याका रूपमा लिई प्रश्नावली र कक्षा अवलोकन उपकरणका माध्यमबाट तथ्य सङ्कलन गरी रचनामुखी र सम्प्रेषणात्मक शिक्षण पद्धतिका आधारमा तथ्य विश्लेषणका साथै निष्कर्ष स्थापित गरिएको छ । तथ्याङ्क विश्लेषणका क्रममा तालिकीकरण, बारम्बारता, प्रतिशताङ्क जस्ता आधार एवम् साक्ष्यका साथ पूर्व अध्येतासँग संवाद गर्दै लेखकीय दृष्टिकोण प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । भाषातत्व अन्तर्गतका अक्षरसंरचना, वर्णविन्यास, पदवर्ग जस्ता पक्षमा आधारित भएर गरिएको यस अध्ययनबाट स्नातक तहमा व्याकरण शिक्षणलाई रचनामुखी, सम्प्रेषणात्मक एवम् व्यावहारिक बनाउने भनिए पनि शिक्षण परम्परागत नियम, परिभाषा र उदाहरण केन्द्रित देखिन्छ । भाषातत्व शिक्षणका क््रmममा पर्याप्त अभ्यास, छलफल, अन्तक्र्रिया, प्रस्तुतीकरण, पृष्ठपोषण जस्ता रचनामुखी एवम् सम्प्रेषणात्मक विधिमा आधारित भएर गरिने शिक्षण कार्य यस तहमा ५० प्रतिशतभन्दा कम भएको देखिन्छ । , ,, ,  ।
american_english: The present research article titled 'Nepali Vyakaran Shikshan Prakriyako Nirupan' ('Exposition of the Nepali Grammar Teaching Process') is a condensed and revised form of the mini research report titled 'Snatok Tahlama Vyakaran Shikshan Prakriyako Avastha' ('The State of Grammar Teaching at the Bachelor's Level'), written by the researcher himself. This article aims to identify the state of grammar teaching at the bachelor's level and to establish whether the said teaching process is conducted in the constructivist and communicative manner directed by the Bachelor's Nepali Teaching Guidelines (2066 BS) and the Bachelor's Nepali Curriculum (2069 BS). Since this article, grounded in a single truth, is of a qualitative-quantitative nature, ten teachers teaching at the bachelor's level in Kaski district and ten classes associated with their grammar teaching were taken as the sample population, data were collected through a questionnaire and a classroom observation instrument, and conclusions were established on the basis of data analysis following constructivist and communicative teaching methods. In the course of data analysis, along with bases and evidence such as tabulation, frequency and percentages, the author's own viewpoint has been presented in dialogue with previous researchers. From this study, carried out on the basis of aspects falling under the elements of language such as syllable structure, orthography and word classes, it emerges that, even though grammar teaching at the bachelor's level is said to be made constructivist, communicative and practical, the teaching appears centered on traditional rules, definitions and examples. It is seen that teaching work based on constructivist and communicative methods — sufficient practice, discussion, interaction, presentation and feedback — carried out in the course of teaching the elements of language amounts to less than 50 percent at this level.
british_english: The present research article entitled 'Nepali Vyakaran Shikshan Prakriyako Nirupan' ('Exposition of the Nepali Grammar Teaching Process') is a shortened and revised form of the mini research report entitled 'Snatok Tahlama Vyakaran Shikshan Prakriyako Avastha' ('The Position of Grammar Teaching at Undergraduate Level'), written by the researcher himself. This article aims to ascertain the position of grammar teaching at undergraduate level and to establish whether the said teaching process is being conducted in accordance with the directives of the Bachelor's Nepali Teaching Guidelines (2066 BS) and the Bachelor's Nepali Curriculum (2069 BS), namely in a constructivist and communicative manner. Since this article, founded upon a single truth, is of a qualitative-quantitative character, ten teachers teaching at undergraduate level in Kaski district, together with ten classes associated with their grammar teaching, were taken as the sample population; data were collected by means of a questionnaire and a classroom observation instrument, and conclusions were established on the basis of analysis of the data according to constructivist and communicative teaching methods. In the course of data analysis, alongside bases and evidence such as tabulation, frequency and percentages, the author's own stance has been presented in dialogue with earlier scholars. From this study, conducted by reference to aspects falling under the elements of language — syllable structure, orthography and word class — it emerges that, even though grammar teaching at this level is said to be rendered constructivist, communicative and practical, the teaching still appears centred upon traditional rules, definitions and examples. It appears that teaching based upon constructivist and communicative methods — sufficient practice, discussion, interaction, presentation and feedback — carried out in the course of teaching the elements of language accounts for less than 50 per cent at this level.
australian_english: The present research article titled 'Nepali Vyakaran Shikshan Prakriyako Nirupan' ('Exposition of the Nepali Grammar Teaching Process') is a shortened and updated version of the mini research report titled 'Snatok Tahlama Vyakaran Shikshan Prakriyako Avastha' ('The State of Grammar Teaching at the Bachelor's Level'), written by the researcher himself. This article sets out to work out the state of grammar teaching at the bachelor's level and to establish whether that teaching process is being run in line with what the Bachelor's Nepali Teaching Guidelines (2066 BS) and the Bachelor's Nepali Curriculum (2069 BS) direct, that is, in a constructivist and communicative manner. Because this article, grounded in a single truth, is of a qualitative-quantitative nature, ten teachers teaching at the bachelor's level in Kaski district and ten classes connected with their grammar teaching were taken as the sample population; data were collected through a questionnaire and a classroom observation tool, and conclusions were drawn on the basis of analysing the data according to constructivist and communicative teaching methods. In the course of analysing the data, alongside bases and evidence like tabulation, frequency and percentages, the author's own view has been put forward in dialogue with earlier researchers. This study, which was carried out on the basis of aspects falling under the elements of language such as syllable structure, spelling and word classes, shows that, even though grammar teaching at the bachelor's level is supposed to be made constructivist, communicative and practical, the teaching still comes across as centred on traditional rules, definitions and examples. It turns out that the teaching done using constructivist and communicative methods — enough practice, discussion, interaction, presentation and feedback — in the course of teaching the elements of language is less than 50 per cent at this level.
informal_english: The research article that's headed 'Nepali Vyakaran Shikshan Prakriyako Nirupan' ('Exposition of the Nepali Grammar Teaching Process') is really just a shortened, tidied-up version of a mini research report the researcher himself wrote called 'Snatok Tahlama Vyakaran Shikshan Prakriyako Avastha' ('The State of Grammar Teaching at the Bachelor's Level'). The article sets out to figure out how grammar teaching stands at the bachelor's level, and whether it's actually done the way the Bachelor's Nepali Teaching Guidelines (2066 BS) and the Bachelor's Nepali Curriculum (2069 BS) lay down — that is, in a constructivist, communicative way. Sure, the piece is grounded in a single truth and it's a qualitative-quantitative kind of study, so for the sample they took ten bachelor's-level teachers in Kaski district and ten classes tied to their grammar teaching, gathered the facts with a questionnaire and a classroom observation tool, and established the conclusions by analysing the facts along constructivist and communicative lines. During the analysis, with things like tabulation, frequency and percentages as the basis and evidence, the author put forward his own viewpoint in dialogue with earlier scholars. Now, the study itself looks at the bits that fall under language elements, like syllable structure, orthography and word classes, and here's the thing: even though bachelor's grammar teaching is supposed to be made constructivist, communicative and practical, the teaching still looks dead set on old-style rules, definitions and examples. And when it comes to actually teaching the language elements with constructivist and communicative methods — practice, discussion, interaction, presentations, feedback and the like — that work comes to less than 50 per cent at this level, and that's a fact.
